html:
A civil war in Chad that began with tax riots in the east in 1965 and grew into a revolt of the Muslim north and east against the southern-led government of Tombalbaye.

The rebel front FROLINAT was founded in Sudan in 1966. France sent troops from 1968. Libya backed the rebels and in 1973 occupied the Aouzou Strip in the far north. After Tombalbaye's death the northern factions of Goukouni Oueddei and Hissene Habre split, and in 1979 fighting destroyed N'Djamena and ended southern rule. Wars among northern factions went on through the 1980s, ending in the Toyota War. See also Gaddafi.
sum: A civil war in Chad that began with tax riots in the east in 1965 and grew into a revolt of the Muslim north and east against the southern-led government of Tombalbaye.
